Legal Standards.name: Delta Reform Act
Legal Standards.note: Establishes overarching state policy and governance framework for the Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta, including requirements affecting freshwater Delta exports.

Legal Standards.name: Bay-Delta Water Quality Control Plan (Bay-Delta Plan)
Legal Standards.note: Defines water quality objectives and beneficial uses for the Bay-Delta; serves as a foundational document in the legal hierarchy governing Delta exports.

Legal Standards.name: Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act
Legal Standards.note: California’s primary water quality law authorizing regulation and enforcement of surface and groundwater quality standards in the Delta.

Legal Standards.name: California Water Code
Legal Standards.note: Statutory framework governing water rights, allocation, and administration, operating alongside Porter-Cologne and Delta-specific mandates.

Legal Standards.name: Federal Clean Water Act (CWA)
Legal Standards.note: Provides the federal legal basis for water quality standards applicable to Delta waters, with EPA oversight of state-adopted standards.

Legal Standards.name: Endangered Species Act (ESA)
Legal Standards.note: Imposes additional federal constraints on Delta operations to protect listed species, affecting freshwater export conditions.

Legal Standards.name: Tiered Agricultural Salinity Threshold (Above Legal Standard)
Legal Standards.note: A tiered water quality threshold that is more protective than the baseline legal standard for agricultural beneficial uses.

key_elements.plain_definition: Electrical Conductivity (EC); averaging period: 14-day average; threshold: <= 450 µS/cm; applicable water years: Most water years; locations: Jersey Point, Emmaton, Rock Slough
Additional water quality standards apply for municipal and industrial (M&I) uses.

Tier 1.threshold: Max(EM, JP) below 900 uS/cm for >=75% of months and above 2500 uS/cm for <=5% of months.

policies.policy_name: Freshwater for Delta Exports / salinity standards
policies.note: All scenarios analyzed fall in Tier 1; Delta export standards are maintained even under the most extreme current conditions.

policies.policy_name: Water rights curtailments & seawater intrusion barriers
policies.note: May be implemented depending on observed conditions, even at Tier 1, because the state's legal threshold is lower than this tier.

Tier 2.threshold: Max(EM, JP) below 900 uS/cm for >=65% of months, below 1600 uS/cm for >=75% of months, and above 2500 uS/cm for <=12% of months.

policies.policy_name: Freshwater for Delta Exports / salinity standards
policies.note: Observed salinity at Emmaton and Jersey Point during extremely dry years aligns with this tier. Reflects drought conditions familiar to the state without significantly impacting export quality.

policies.policy_name: Water rights curtailments & seawater intrusion barriers
policies.note: Curtailments and salinity barriers would almost certainly be implemented at this tier.

policies.policy_name: TUCP/O salinity standards relaxation under SWRCB D-1641
policies.note: Water Code & SWRCB regulations allow temporary relaxation of salinity standards in these conditions.

Tier 3.threshold: Max(EM, JP) below 900 uS/cm for >=55% of months, below 1600 uS/cm for >=65% of months, and above 2500 uS/cm for <=20% of months.

policies.policy_name: Freshwater for Delta Exports / salinity standards
policies.note: Salinity levels exceed those currently experienced; water management could mitigate somewhat but likely cannot meet current standards.
More water treatment required, further reducing available supply under Tier 3 conditions.

policies.policy_name: TUCP/O salinity standards relaxation under SWRCB D-1641
policies.note: Temporary relaxation of salinity standards continues to allow operations under extreme conditions.

policies.policy_name: Water rights curtailments & seawater intrusion barriers
policies.note: Measures from previous tiers remain in place.

Tier 4.threshold: Max(EM, JP) below 900 uS/cm for <55% of months and/or above 2500 uS/cm for >20% of months.

policies.policy_name: Freshwater for Delta Exports / salinity standards
policies.note: Critical salinity levels persist for much of the year, representing unprecedented drought and water quality challenges.
Project water deliveries may cease except for basic food and water security; conditions could persist for several years.
Regions and localities would be required to use reserved water currently being set aside to maintain survival-level supply.
